Naomi — quick read from pricing/strategy: we can do structured protection for customers but it needs to be narrow and tied to clearly defined GPU-index movements. Options that are realistic from our side:

- 12 months: standard reserved discount (baseline) + no price-sensitivity clause. Good for straightforward commit but higher short-term discount than 24m.
- 18 months: we can offer a modest incremental discount (approx +6% vs 12m) if we include a "price-sensitivity collar" — i.e., if GPU market average (monthly) increases >20% vs baseline, OrbitAI can claim a credit equal to X% of monthly spend (proposal below).
- 24 months: best unit economics for us; we can increase discount further (approx +12% vs 12m) but we are unlikely to accept an automatic re-price; instead we'd propose a capped true-up/credit (up to 10% of monthly invoice) linked to an agreed vendor GPU index.

Proposal for the collar (draft for approval):
- Baseline index: average of major GPU contract prices in the 30 days before signature (we'll propose vendor index partners).
- Trigger: sustained 30-day increase > 20% relative to baseline.
- Remedy: for the months where index > trigger, customer gets a credit equal to (index-increase% * 0.5) * monthly reserved spend, capped at 10% of that month’s invoice.

This preserves our economics (we absorb half the delta up to cap) and gives procurement a concrete remedy. Kicker: any credit applied is non-refundable and is applied against future usage invoices or held as a credit pool for 6 months.

Approval path: anything with net discount delta >10% or caps >10% of monthly invoice needs Senior Finance + COO sign-off. Discounts within 10% can be approved by Sales + Finance lead.

I can model a couple of scenarios (12/18/24m) with the Orbit workbook — Marcus, can you confirm operational sizing assumptions so we don't over-reserve?

-Karthik

Thanks — added an ops lens. Key points from infra/runtime:

- OrbitAI forecast summary (from attached): steady-state ~140 A100-equivalent, peak 1.6x => provisioning target = 225 A100-equivalent peak (to be safe on burst routing).
- We can service bursts with a hybrid approach: reserve core pool sized to ~160 A100-equivalent (this covers steady-state + 15% buffer) and allow controlled burst on a shared burst pool with pre-negotiated burst credits. That means reserved commitment is smaller (160 vs 225) and we preserve headroom without forcing OrbitAI to reserve the full peak.
- Operational requirements: a burst-capacity SLA, clear throttling/fairness policy, and a short lead time (48–72 hours) to spin up additional dedicated instances when shared pool capacity is available.
- Cost delta: reserving 160 vs 225 reduces committed spend by ~29% while still meeting latency SLOs for 95% of traffic (we'll absorb a small tail with burst ops).

If OrbitAI wants guaranteed full 225 reserved, that's a heavier discount ask and will likely push approval to execs. Marcus suggests we model two commercial offers:
A) 18-month, reserve 160 (with burst credits), 10% discount, price-sensitivity collar as Karthik proposed (cap 10%).
B) 24-month, reserve 225 (no burst reliance), 15% discount, limited collar (credits capped at 5% monthly) — but this triggers Senior Finance + COO approval.

I've sketched expected GPU-equivalent headcount and ops procedures — attaching a short CSV with the sizing math (pricing-breakdown-ORBIT-5421.csv).

-Marcus
Director, Serving & Operations
